transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-02 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (CSM), Diego Rivera (SE) — Aisha Khan (Maple Harbor), Tom Becker (SRE), Mei Chen (Security)

Summary:
Quick op-orientation: confirm SLAs for production ramp, telemetry and observability exports, and final checklist for VPC/on-prem pilot. Action items captured at end.

Topics: SLA thresholds, observability hooks, metric retention, VPC connectivity, compliance docs, pilot timeline

[00:00] Jordan Ellis: All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Hi this is Aisha — Head of Platform at Maple Harbor, TL;DR we're evaluating Redwood Dedicated and maybe a private deployment later, want to confirm telemetry and SLA bits.
[00:18] Jordan Ellis: Great thanks Aisha. I'm Jordan, AE — Priya's CSM — Diego is our SE who will run the telemetry and runbook pieces.
[00:27] Diego Rivera: Hey -- hi all, Diego here.
[00:30] Tom Becker: Tom, SRE Manager. We run the inference for route optimization and need predictable latency under 120ms p95.
[00:38] Mei Chen: Mei from security, I'll be validating SOC 2 and encryption for the pilot.
[00:43] Jordan Ellis: Cool. Agenda: SLA confirmation for Dedicated, what telemetry we can push into your prometheus stack, required network flow for VPC peering, and next steps.

[00:58] Priya Nair: Quick note — we did a preliminary perf run, but that was on shared capacity; Dedicated numbers are different. We'll share the dedicated-perf baseline doc after this call.

[01:20] Tom Becker: Sounds good. On the latency target: 120ms p95 is the bar. What's realistic for your Dedicated pools at our QPS (about 150 qps at peak)?
[01:33] Diego Rivera: So for 150 QPS with seq len around 256, Dedicated with our optimized kernels usually lands around 70-110ms p95; that aligns but we need definitive benchmarks. We can run a targeted perf test on a reserved pool.
[01:52] Aisha Khan: Would that test be in our VPC or yours?
[01:56] Diego Rivera: Preferably in your VPC for the most realistic network latency. We can spin a small dedicated pool in the region and run the harness.

[02:15] Mei Chen: On compliance — we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a contact person to validate controls. Also, how does Redwood handle KM S keys — are they customer-managed?
[02:28] Jordan Ellis: Good question. We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed via KMS for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted there are limitations. I'll attach the KMS integration doc.
[02:40] Mei Chen: Perfect, please include the HSM/HSM support note if available.

[02:50] Tom Becker: Telemetry — we use Prometheus and Grafana. Can Redwood stream metrics into our scrape targets or do we need to pull from Redwood endpoints?
[03:02] Diego Rivera: Two options: push-based exports (we can forward metrics to your pushgateway via TLS) or you scrape our metrics endpoint over the peered link. Scrape is simpler if you want Prometheus-native metrics. We also support exporting traces (Zipkin/OpenTelemetry).
[03:21] Aisha Khan: If you expose a scrape endpoint, can we control metric retention? We prefer not to pull raw request payloads.
[03:29] Diego Rivera: Yes, you control retention in your Prometheus; Redwood can emit aggregated metrics only — token counts, latency buckets, error rates, model-version labels, but not full request bodies. We'll redact or not export sensitive fields.

[03:48] Priya Nair: Note: the default telemetry retention on Redwood Console is 90 days, but for Dedicated you can extend to longer via an add-on.

[04:02] Aisha Khan: OK that's helpful. For our compliance team we also need audit logs of token access and admin actions for 12 months.
[04:11] Jordan Ellis: For Dedicated and Private we provide audit logs export, can ship them to your S3 or to your SIEM via secure transfer. We'll capture admin user actions, API key usage, and model rollout events.
[04:26] Mei Chen: Does audit log include token-level cost data? We need to reconcile spend.
[04:33] Jordan Ellis: We include token counts and cost metrics in the billing exports; exact PII-free breakdown can be included.

[04:45] Tom Becker: Networking: what are the firewall ports and IPs for VPC peering?
[04:51] Diego Rivera: We'll provide a single CIDR and a small list of endpoints. For peering we do cross-account VPC peering in the same cloud provider or IPsec for on-prem. Ports: 443 for control plane, gRPC port for inference (we'll give exact port in the network doc).
[05:07] Aisha Khan: Note: our security policy needs separate NAT and no public IPs on hosts. Can you support that?
[05:13] Diego Rivera: Yes 100%. We support customer-managed NAT and no public IPs for nodes in a private deployment.

[05:25] Speaker 1: (murmur) can we also look at autoscaling behavior?
[05:29] Jordan Ellis: Autoscaling for Dedicated is policy-driven. You can set target QPS or latency SLOs; there's also burst capacity. Diego will share our autoscaler config examples.

[05:46] Tom Becker: For the pilot, can we start with one model and then add reranking/embedding endpoints?
[05:52] Diego Rivera: Absolutely. Start with a single model variant, pin the version, and then can stage the rerank/embedding lanes. We recommend starting with a small cache TTL and then adjust once traffic shapes are stable.

[06:10] Aisha Khan: About caching — does Redwood do prefix caching automatically? We want to avoid inconsistent responses when using caching plus user-specific context.
[06:21] Diego Rivera: We support both prefix/KV caching and per-customer caching policies. You can configure cache keying to include or exclude user identifiers. We'll share the caching config examples.

[06:36] Priya Nair: I also wanted to flag that our onboarding playbook has a checklist: network, perf test, telemetry, compliance handoff, pilot run, and go/no-go. We'll run the playbook with your team.

[06:52] Mei Chen: Quick Q — encryption at rest for model artifacts and logs?
[06:56] Jordan Ellis: Encrypted at rest with AES-256, customer-managed KMS optional for Private and Dedicated.

[07:05] Tom Becker: Regarding SLOs — you mentioned automatic fallback policies. If a model variant fails, what's the expected failover time?
[07:14] Diego Rivera: Fallback is in the order of seconds — automatic fallback to compatible variant or to hosted pool depending on your policy. We also have circuit-breaker thresholds that avoid rapid flip-flopping.

[07:29] Aisha Khan: For billing — we want per-route cost reporting. Can you provide token-level CSV exports?
[07:36] Jordan Ellis: Yes we provide per-route/per-model token breakdowns with timestamps and costs. We can send daily exports into your billing S3.

[07:50] Speaker 2 (Tom): Any limitation on model quantization? We plan to use a quantized TGI fork.
[07:59] Diego Rivera: We support common quantization formats; we recommend a validation pass because some custom quant builds can change numerical behavior. We'll run an eval on a small prompt set.

[08:15] Aisha Khan: Timeline question — if we sign the Dedicated contract this month, when can pilot in prod-like environment start?
[08:24] Jordan Ellis: Typically 4–6 weeks: 1 week for contract & procurement, 2 weeks for environment provisioning and networking, 1–2 weeks for perf testing and pilot validation.

[08:39] Mei Chen: Procurement will need the standard MSA and DPAs. Any gotchas?
[08:44] Jordan Ellis: We'll send standard MSA and DPA; for specialized SSO or data residency requirements we can amend. Priya will coordinate with procurement.

[08:56] Tom Becker: Are there rate limits or quotas during pilot?
[09:00] Priya Nair: For pilot we usually set soft quotas and can lift them after safety checks; we'll put explicit limits in the sandbox to avoid noisy neighbors.

[09:11] Aisha Khan: Good. I want to check specifics about telemetry metrics names — can you give a short example?
[09:18] Diego Rivera: Example metrics: redwood_inference_requests_total{model="m-optim-1",route="/v1/generate"}, redwood_inference_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood_cache_hit_ratio, redwood_kv_cache_usage_bytes.
[09:35] Mei Chen: That 'kv cache' text — we've seen it as 'key value cash' in other docs — just making sure it's key-value cache.
[09:42] Diego Rivera: Yep, key-value cache — sorry for the transcript quirk if any.

[09:50] Speaker 3 (Jordan): We'll redact any request body fields by default; payloads are not exported to Prometheus.

[10:00] Tom Becker: Ok let's talk about an actual test. Diego said you'd run perf harness in our VPC. What credentials do you need?
[10:07] Diego Rivera: We'll need a temporary test role or a bastion flow, or we can connect via a peered link. Ideally you provide an IAM role with limited permissions for provisioning test hosts. We'll also need a whitelisted egress for our CI agents.

[10:24] Aisha Khan: We can prod a short-lived role. I'll have Tom handle that.

[10:29] Tom Becker: Fine. We'll also need step-by-step runbook so our on-call knows expected behavior during pilot.
[10:36] Priya Nair: Diego and I will co-author the runbook: expected alerts, runbook steps for failover, and escalation path. We'll include runbook links in the follow-up email.

[10:48] Mei Chen: A couple of security clarifications: are access tokens rotated automatically? And what's the default TTL?
[10:55] Jordan Ellis: Tokens can be auto-rotated; default TTL is 30 days but you can request shorter. For Dedicated we recommend short-lived credentials with long-lived service principals for infra automation.

[11:09] Aisha Khan: For the demo sequence — Diego, can you show a quick example of the telemetry dashboard?
[11:14] Diego Rivera: I can share screen but given this is a call recording we'll instead point to a saved sample dashboard. I'll include a link in the email. Sample shows latency p50/p95, cache-hit ratio, QPS by model.

[11:28] Tom Becker: Perfect. Anything about backups for model artifacts?
[11:33] Diego Rivera: Model artifacts are versioned and backed up; for Private deployments we can also snapshot and push to your S3.

[11:44] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[11:46] Priya Nair: We're tracking open items in our onboarding tracker, but main blockers from customer side were SOC 2 contact and environment diagram.

[12:00] Aisha Khan: I'll send environment diagram today and the SOC 2 contact by EOD tomorrow.

[12:07] Mei Chen: I'll send the compliance point of contact and the list of required artifacts.

[12:12] Jordan Ellis: Great. To recap — Redwood to share: tailored SLA PDF and pricing sheet, network peering doc, autoscaler config, telemetry examples and sample dashboards, and perf harness plan. Maple Harbor to share: environment diagram, SOC 2 contact, approval timeline for procurement.

[12:35] Tom Becker: One more technical nit: do you support mutual TLS between our ingress and the inference nodes for extra security?
[12:42] Diego Rivera: Yes mutual TLS is supported for Private and Dedicated modes; we'll include setup steps in the network doc.

[12:52] Aisha Khan: Are there any known limitations with GPU types — we use A-series in prod.
[12:58] Diego Rivera: We support a variety of GPU families; we'll match the kernel selection to the GPU. For A-series we'll validate performance during the perf run.

[13:12] Priya Nair: I'll send calendar invite for the runbook review and perf window next Tuesday.

[13:19] Jordan Ellis: Next steps folks — quick recap I will send follow-up with attachments and links. Diego will coordinate perf tests and runbook. Priya will handle procurement docs. Aisha and Mei will share environment and compliance contacts.

[13:34] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[13:38] Diego Rivera: None, just need the VPC diagram and a temp role.

[13:43] Tom Becker: Ok we'll get that to you.

[13:46] Jordan Ellis: Great thanks everyone. We'll send the note-out and action items within 24 hours.

[13:53] --- End meeting transcript (note: transcription imperfect; some product names may be transcribed incorrectly, e.g., KV cache as "key value cash")

Recap (short):
- Pilot timeline estimated 4–6 weeks after contract; perf harness in customer VPC recommended.
- Telemetry options: scrape endpoint or pushgateway; data exported is aggregated only.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and KMS options discussed.
- Action items assigned; follow-up email to include SLA, network doc, autoscaler examples, perf schedule.
